signature_moves: Zed idiom on native bones: ports Zed/VS-Code dark-editor grammar (activity-view sidebar switcher, closable tabs, bottom terminal/git/debug drawer, Zed-compatible themes) into a genuine AppKit window — Themes pane literally credits Zed
Fixed brand-violet accent (~#8B7CC8) binds primary buttons/focus/active-tab/selected-card/md-headings — cohesive but overrides the user's system accent
Inverted-depth graphite: 3-step tonal stack where chrome (#393B45) > canvas (#282934) > terminal/theme-cards (#0B0A0E); depth by tone, not shadow or glass
Per-language full-colour file-type iconography (php/Go/Rust/Kotlin/Swift/JS/TS/CSS/npm/toml/md) where native browsers use monochrome Finder icons
defects: Contrast Dilution (structural) — tab-bar edges, pane outlines and Settings-card borders sit under 3:1 on graphite; grouping survives by fill-step not visible edge. Fix: dark separators from Fills tiers to ~3:1
Selection grammar deviation (native tell #3) — sidebar active file = bold weight only, no inset rounded accent fill / no accent glyph; Zed-style current-doc indicator, excluded from macOS canon
Accent not bound to controlAccentColor (native tell #6) — fixed brand violet; consistent but non-native
Line Length Fatigue (soft) — Settings card descriptions run ~100ch (editor prose is user content, less culpable)
Dense action cluster — Terminal panel header packs ~6-7 icon actions tightly (borderline crowding, monochrome keeps it below Focal Collision)

aesthetic.direction: Neo-grotesque product-dark / dev-IDE (Zed idiom): dark cool-graphite neutral ramp + one electric-violet accent, dense-calm layout, subtle (too-subtle) borders, Dracula-family syntax — the current default-model dev-tool look, chosen here with genuine reason (it IS a code editor)

psychology: Jakob's Law — heavily exploited: file tree + closable tabs + bottom terminal/git panel + status bar reproduce VS-Code/Zed conventions so developers arrive already trained; muscle memory is the whole value prop
Aesthetic-Usability Effect — cohesive violet-on-graphite dark theme + per-language icons raise perceived usability/quality on first contact
Von Restorff (isolation) — the single filled-violet primary among grey/disabled controls (Save Profile) is the one remembered, correct action-singularity
Hick's Law — Settings split into 10 focused nav sections + a search field keeps each decision point small; editor chrome stays minimal
Miller/Cowan chunking — bottom drawer chunks tooling into 3 modes (terminal/git/debug) behind one switcher
External-consistency cost (Jakob, mild violation) — the fixed brand accent ignores the user's chosen system accent, a small break from platform-trained expectation
notes: All 6 shots are the same app, dark mode only, @2x retina (2880x1800 raw = 1440pt window). No light-mode, empty-state, onboarding, or menu evidence. Cover.jpg is a marketing composite (violet/indigo gradient backdrop, heavy grotesque 'Inkline' display, glass app-icon render, 'BUILT FOR macOS / APPKIT NATIVE' badges) — brand evidence only; the icon and backdrop are NOT UI evidence (icon reserved for Workflow B). Lineage is native/med: chrome is unmistakably AppKit (genuine traffic lights, centred proxy-icon+POSIX-path title, native pop-up buttons, System UI font) and there are zero Electron tells, but the entire interior is custom-drawn in the cross-platform-editor idiom, so a native-shell-around-a-web-editor cannot be fully ruled out from stills — do not learn the interior tab/sidebar/panel grammar as mac canon. Accent-hex is estimated (button has a gradient + white label; sampling averaged them). Structural border colours are the weakest link (Contrast Dilution). Settings window is the strongest, most native surface — closest to canon-eligible.
